answer_sql:
WITH ord AS (
  SELECT
    l.order_key,
    s.country_code AS store_cc,
    c.country_code AS cust_cc,
    SUM(l.net_amount) AS order_value
  FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS l
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_store AS s
    ON l.store_key = s.store_key
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_customer AS c
    ON l.customer_key = c.customer_key
  GROUP BY
    l.order_key,
    s.country_code,
    c.country_code
), shop AS (
  SELECT
    store_cc AS cc,
    COUNT(*) AS orders,
    AVG(order_value) AS aov
  FROM ord
  WHERE
    store_cc <> '--'
  GROUP BY
    store_cc
  HAVING
    AVG(order_value) > 500
), buyer AS (
  SELECT
    cust_cc AS cc,
    COUNT(*) AS orders,
    AVG(order_value) AS aov
  FROM ord
  WHERE
    cust_cc <> '--'
  GROUP BY
    cust_cc
  HAVING
    AVG(order_value) > 500
)
SELECT
  d.country_name AS country,
  s.orders AS orders_if_country_means_the_shop,
  ROUND(s.aov, 2) AS avg_order_value_if_country_means_the_shop,
  b.orders AS orders_if_country_means_the_buyer,
  ROUND(b.aov, 2) AS avg_order_value_if_country_means_the_buyer
FROM shop AS s
FULL OUTER JOIN buyer AS b
  ON s.cc = b.cc
JOIN contoso_served.dim_country AS d
  ON d.country_code = COALESCE(s.cc, b.cc)
ORDER BY
  avg_order_value_if_country_means_the_buyer DESC

body.value: The 8 countries whose typical order is worth more than 500 USD — which is every country Contoso sells in — each shown with the two candidate figures I refuse to merge: what one order averages if the country means the shop that sold it, and what it averages if the country means where the buyer lives. Both are the average value of a single order after discount, in USD, across all ten years of orders on record. The table does NOT give one reconciled figure per country, because averaging the two readings or picking between them silently is precisely what the governing ruling prohibits; and nothing here is restricted by order status, converted out of USD, limited to a date window, or filtered by a minimum order count.

value:
All 8 countries qualify either way — so the only thing I need from you is which country an order should belong to: the country of the shop that sold it, or the country the buyer lives in? Point at one column.

                   (A) country = THE SHOP      (B) country = THE BUYER
  Italy                 2,617.62 (1,760)          2,459.71 (2,669)
  United Kingdom        2,498.53 (6,027)          2,413.06 (9,552)
  United States         2,430.24 (27,910)         2,356.13 (47,477)
  Germany               2,427.47 (5,925)          2,319.60 (10,622)
  Canada                2,396.95 (5,721)          2,307.13 (10,074)
  Australia             2,348.50 (3,194)          2,288.96 (5,837)
  France                2,272.68 (1,638)          2,250.41 (2,966)
  Netherlands           2,239.53 (2,327)          2,204.90 (4,273)
                        54,502 orders             93,470 orders

Average value of one order in USD, after discount, over all orders ever: 2016-05-18 to 2025-12-31. Order counts in brackets.

(A) "where we trade" — orders rung up by physical shops in that country. The web shop is NOT in this column at all: its country is recorded as a sentinel, not a place.
(B) "where our customers are" — orders placed by customers resident in that country, wherever they bought, web shop included.

WHAT YOUR CHOICE DOES NOT CHANGE: the same 8 countries qualify, in the identical rank order, Italy highest and the Netherlands lowest. The "exceeds 500" test does no work at all — the lowest average anywhere is 2,204.90, over four times the bar, and nothing is borderline. Reading the money before discount instead of after lifts every figure about 6.3% and still excludes nobody.

WHAT IT DOES CHANGE: whether the web shop is in the answer — 38,968 orders carrying 86,790,054.13, 42% of all orders and 40% of all revenue, present in (B) and absent from (A); and each country's figure, by 1.0% (France) to 6.4% (Italy), (A) higher throughout.

NEEDING NO DECISION: attributing an order to the country of the SITE the shop stands on gives column (A) exactly — the site's country and the shop's country disagree on 0 of the 93,470 orders.

No single figure is claimed, so there are two populations and neither is offered as THE answer. (A) the shop reading: 54,502 orders, each rung up at a physical shop sited in one of the 8 real countries — EXCLUDING 38,968 online orders, because the web shop's store and site country is the '--' sentinel and country.exclusion.sentinel_is_not_a_country forbids reporting it as a ninth country; these 8 country totals sum to 132,024,417.5, matching the declared physical-channel figure. (B) the buyer reading: all 93,470 orders, none excluded, each attributed to the country its customer lives in; these 8 country totals sum to 218,814,471.66, matching the declared both-channel figure to the cent. Common to both, and verified on these rows: the grain is the order (distinct order_key, 93,470 behind 223,974 lines, each order carrying exactly one customer, store and date), the money is net_amount after discount in USD, the period is the full extent of order_date 2016-05-18 to 2025-12-31 with no date limit, both channels are in scope as populations (no `physical` subject-default applied, the subject being a measure and not a Store), and NO order is dropped for being cancelled, refunded or unpaid — not by my choice but because this bundle records no status, payment or refund column at all. The '--' sentinel is excluded from the country list under both readings, and no minimum-order-count floor was imposed; none was needed, the thinnest base being France's 1,638 orders.

WITH o AS (
  SELECT
    order_key,
    customer_key,
    store_key,
    SUM(net_amount) AS order_value
  FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line
  GROUP BY
    order_key,
    customer_key,
    store_key
), attributed AS (
  SELECT
    o.order_value,
    s.country_code AS store_cc,
    c.country_code AS cust_cc,
    l.country_code AS loc_cc
  FROM o
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_store AS s
    ON o.store_key = s.store_key
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_customer AS c
    ON o.customer_key = c.customer_key
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_location AS l
    ON s.location_code = l.location_code
), per_country AS (
  SELECT
    'store' AS reading,
    store_cc AS cc,
    AVG(order_value) AS aov
  FROM attributed
  GROUP BY
    store_cc
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    'customer',
    cust_cc,
    AVG(order_value)
  FROM attributed
  GROUP BY
    cust_cc
)
SELECT
  (
    SELECT
      COUNT(*)
    FROM attributed
    WHERE
      store_cc <> loc_cc
  ) AS orders_where_store_differs_from_location,
  (
    SELECT
      COUNT(*)
    FROM attributed
    WHERE
      store_cc <> cust_cc
  ) AS orders_where_store_differs_from_customer,
  reading,
  COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE
    cc <> '--') AS real_countries,
  COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE
    cc <> '--' AND aov > 500) AS real_countries_above_500,
  COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE
    cc <> '--' AND aov <= 500) AS real_countries_at_or_below_500,
  ROUND(MIN(aov) FILTER(WHERE
    cc <> '--'), 2) AS lowest_country_aov,
  ROUND(MAX(aov) FILTER(WHERE
    cc <> '--'), 2) AS highest_country_aov
FROM per_country
GROUP BY
  reading
ORDER BY
  reading
